function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below are the most common ways to pull *detailed* information about a network interface (e.g., eth0, enp2s0, wlan0) on a typical Linux host. Feel free to replace `` with the name of the interface you’re interested in. | Tool | What it shows | Typical command | |------|---------------|-----------------| | **`ip`** | Interface state, MAC address, MTU, IP addresses, flags, traffic counters | `ip link show `
`ip addr show ` | | **`ethtool`** | Driver name & version, firmware revision, supported/advertised speeds, duplex, autonegotiation, link partner capabilities, statistics, EEPROM contents | `ethtool -i `
`ethtool -S `
`ethtool -a `
`ethtool -m ` | | **`lshw`** | Full hardware description (driver, bus info, physical location, vendor/product IDs, serial number, configuration options) | `sudo lshw -class network -short`
`sudo lshw -class network -numeric` | | **`nmcli`** | NetworkManager‑managed device properties (state, connection, speed, MAC, IPv4/IPv6 config, DNS, routes) | `nmcli device show ` | | **`ifconfig`** *(legacy)* | Basic interface info (IP, netmask, broadcast, flags, RX/TX bytes) | `ifconfig ` | | **`cat /sys/class/net//device/...`** | Low‑level sysfs attributes (bus info, PCI ID, IRQ, DMA, power state) | `cat /sys/class/net//device/vendor`
`cat /sys/class/net//device/device` | ### Quick “one‑liner” examples ```bash # 1. Show all basic info + IP addresses ip -details -statistics link show # 2. Get driver & firmware details ethtool -i # 3. Dump all available statistics counters ethtool -S # 4. List supported speeds & duplex modes ethtool -k # 5. Show full hardware tree (requires root) sudo lshw -class network -numeric # 6. Query NetworkManager for current connection profile nmcli device show ``` ### What each command gives you | Command | Key output fields | |---------|-------------------| | `ip link show ` | `state UP/DOWN`, `link/ether `, `mtu `, `flags`, `rx/tx queue sizes` | | `ip addr show ` | `inet /`, `inet6 /`, `scope global/local`, `valid_lft`, `preferred_lft` | | `ethtool -i ` | `driver`, `version`, `firmware-version`, `bus-info`, `supports-statistics`, `supports-test`, `supports-eeprom-access` | | `ethtool -S ` | All counters: `rx_packets`, `tx_packets`, `rx_bytes`, `tx_bytes`, `rx_errors`, `tx_errors`, `collisions`, `rx_dropped`, `tx_dropped`, … | | `lshw -class network -numeric` | `product`, `vendor`, `physical id`, `serial`, `configuration` (`driver=...`, `link type=Ethernet`, `speed=1000Mb/s`, `duplex=full`) | | `nmcli device show ` | `GENERAL.STATE`, `GENERAL.CONNECTION`, `IP4.ADDRESS[1]`, `IP6.ADDRESS[1]`, `IP4.GATEWAY`, `IP6.GATEWAY`, `IP4.DNS`, `IP6.DNS`, `DEVICE`, `TYPE`, `STATE`, `CONNECTION.ID`, `CONNECTION.PATH` | --- #### Example walk‑through Suppose you want to know why your `enp2s0` interface is down: ```bash $ ip link show enp2s0 2: enp2s0: mtu 1500 qdisc pfifo_fast state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000 link/ether 00:11:22:33:44:55 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff $ ethtool -i enp2s0 driver: e1000e version: 3.2.6-k firmware-version: 0.13-3 bus-info: 0000:02:00.0 supports-statistics: yes supports-test: yes supports-eeprom-access: yes supports-register-dump: yes supports-priv-flags: no $ ethtool -S enp2s0 | grep rx_ rx_packets: 123456 rx_bytes: 987654321 rx_errors: 0 rx_dropped: 0 ``` If the interface were actually down, `ip link show` would display `state DOWN`. You could then check the link partner with `ethtool -t enp2s0` or look at the cable/port status in `/sys/class/net/enp2s0/device/`. --- ### On other operating systems | OS | Equivalent command(s) | |----|-----------------------| | **macOS** | `ifconfig ` (basic), `networksetup -getinfo ` (DNS, gateway), `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType` (hardware) | | **Windows** | PowerShell: `Get-NetAdapter -Name ""` (status, MAC, speed), `Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias ""` (IP, DNS, gateway) | --- #### TL;DR 1. **Basic state & IP** → `ip link show ` + `ip addr show ` 2. **Driver & firmware** → `ethtool -i ` 3. **Counters & stats** → `ethtool -S ` 4. **Full hardware tree** → `sudo lshw -class network -numeric` 5. **NetworkManager view** → `nmcli device show ` Pick the one that matches the level of detail you need. If you run into a specific issue (e.g., “link is down but cable is plugged”), let me know and I can help interpret the output!
